note: Hook formulas for narrated explainers and short-form films. Write three hooks from three different formulas, score them with `python scripts/studio.py hook score`, then pick. Each entry says what the formula is for and how it gets ruined. `signals` are loose regexes used only to suggest which formula a finished line resembles. Original wording; the 'write several, score, choose' loop and the idea of a formula library come from Jake Schincariol's short-form skills (MIT), see docs/short-form-lessons.md.

formulas.name: Stamped event
formulas.example: Sunday night, October eleventh. Hundreds of French supermarkets threw out everything in their fridges.
formulas.use_when: The event is recent or dated and the date itself adds weight.
formulas.fails_when: The date is the only concrete thing and the stake never arrives.

formulas.name: Number collapse
formulas.template: <Thing> used to take <big number>. Now it takes <small number>.
formulas.example: A database lookup across a billion rows takes four disk reads.
formulas.use_when: Two figures on one axis carry the whole surprise.
formulas.fails_when: The ratio is not believable at a glance, or the two numbers are not comparable.

formulas.name: Nobody did it
formulas.template: Nobody <did the obvious cause>. <The result happened anyway>.
formulas.example: Nobody broke in. The machines had been told to warm up.
formulas.use_when: The cause is more surprising than the outcome.
formulas.fails_when: The twist is not paid off by the next two sentences.

formulas.name: Feature, not bug
formulas.template: The <alarming thing> was <a normal, designed behaviour>.
formulas.example: The weapon was a feature. Every freezer is built to heat its own coils.
formulas.use_when: A mechanism turns out to be the explanation.
formulas.fails_when: The mechanism needs three terms defined before the sentence makes sense.

formulas.name: Myth flip
formulas.template: Everyone thinks <belief>. <The record> says <what is true>.
formulas.example: Everyone blames bad air for cholera. One map of one street pump said otherwise.
formulas.use_when: The belief is genuinely common and the correction is specific.
formulas.fails_when: The belief is a straw man nobody holds.

formulas.name: Human scale
formulas.example: Nearly two trillion dollars. That is about five thousand dollars for every person on Earth.
formulas.use_when: The figure is too large to feel and a comparison makes it land.
formulas.fails_when: The comparison is more abstract than the figure.

formulas.name: One small change
formulas.template: Change <one small thing> and <a large consequence follows>.
formulas.example: Add one server to a cluster and, with the wrong hash, nearly every key moves.
formulas.use_when: The film is about sensitivity or a hidden dependency.
formulas.fails_when: The consequence is not shown in the first visual.

formulas.name: Concrete question
formulas.template: Why does <a specific, visible thing> <do something odd>?
formulas.example: Why does ice float, when almost every other solid sinks in its own liquid?
formulas.use_when: The odd thing can be shown in the first frame.
formulas.fails_when: The question is answered in the next sentence, so there is no investigation.

formulas.name: Small steps, large result
formulas.example: One setting. Eight hours. Hundreds of stores.
formulas.use_when: A cause chain can be said as three beats of three words.
formulas.fails_when: The three beats are not causally linked.

formulas.name: Primary source
formulas.template: "<A short quote from someone who was there>," <who, when>.
formulas.example: "We smelled it before the alarm went," a night technician told investigators.
formulas.use_when: A verified quote carries the stake better than a narrator can.
formulas.fails_when: The quote is unverified or paraphrased into something it did not say.

formulas.name: Before and after
formulas.example: At four degrees the shelves were full. By Monday morning they were in skips.
formulas.use_when: The change of state is the story.
formulas.fails_when: The before-state is generic, so there is nothing to lose.

formulas.name: The rule
formulas.template: There is a rule: <short statement>. Here is why it works.
formulas.example: Divide 72 by the interest rate and you get the years it takes money to double.
formulas.use_when: The film teaches one portable formula or heuristic.
formulas.fails_when: The rule is stated without a first example the viewer can try.
